title: Hierarchical instruction queueing and deadline policies - scratchpad
content:
Context
This is a personal scratchpad to sketch a hierarchical instruction queueing model for our ingress runtime. Goal: reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive lanes while maintaining throughput/cost for bulk/background lanes. Want a flexible, config-driven system so product can define classes (interactive, background, batch, canary) with deadlines, preemption, and soft-priority policies.

Constraints/assumptions
- Requests arrive with metadata (customer_id, route, instruction_type, estimated_tokens, user_priority_hint).
- Serving runtime supports batching and KV-cache warm starts. Batching helps cost but increases latency; we must hedge.
- Some lanes need sub-50ms response SLO; others can tolerate seconds.
- Workload is multi-tenant; tenant-level fairness and reserved capacity exist.

Design goals
- Hierarchical queues: global -> tenant -> lane. Each level can enforce quotas and scheduling policies.
- Deadlines: each request carries a deadline_ms. Scheduler enforces strict fast-path for requests near deadline.
- Preemption: ability to preempt queued non-critical work in favor of imminent-deadline requests. Preemption must be bounded and observable.
- Backpressure signals: caller-side and ingress-side signals (429 vs degraded sampling).
- Graceful batching: allow short hold windows (hold_ms) per lane but with an overriding max_wait for deadline-critical requests.
- Config-driven: product teams supply lane configs; default heuristics for unspecified routes.

API / request metadata (shape thoughts)
- We carry this in a header or JSON payload attribute. Minimal fields are required so SDKs can opt-in. Example JSON envelope: 

{
  "customer_id": "acct_1234",
  "route": "/api/v1/generate",
  "instruction_type": "interactive", 
  "estimated_tokens": 48,
  "deadline_ms": 120,            // ms from now; optional
  "hold_ms_hint": 25,           // preferred batching window (soft)
  "priority_hint": "user:high", // freeform label for routing
  "trace_id": "..."
}

Important: deadline_ms must be honored relative to scheduling time (not arrival) so proxies adding latency are accounted for. If deadline_ms omitted, lane default applies.

Lane config sketch (YAML-ish)
- lanes:
  - name: interactive
    default_deadline_ms: 150
    hold_ms_cap: 40
    preemptible: true
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
    admission_policy:
      token_quota_per_min: 200k
      concurrent_limit: 150
  - name: background
    default_deadline_ms: 8000
    hold_ms_cap: 200
    preemptible: false
    admission_policy:
      token_quota_per_min: 2M
      concurrent_limit: 400

Hierarchy enforcement rules (high level)
- Global admission: ensure system-level available_workers >= min_reserved_pool for interactive. If below, shed background admissions.
- Tenant quotas: a tenant cannot exceed token_quota; excess requests are routed to 'throttled' queue which can be proactively rejected or delayed.
- Lane-level scheduling: queue items are prioritized by expiration_time = arrival_time + deadline_ms. The scheduler picks: earliest expiration first (EDF) but with fairness windows to avoid starvation of bulk lanes.

Preemption model
- Preemption only applies to queued work (not in-progress model inference). For in-progress, rely on faster, cheaper model variants or fallback routing.
- When a high-priority EDF item would miss deadline if waiting, attempt to evict queued items from preemptible lanes to free batch slots. Evicted items either requeue with bumped hold_ms or are rejected with code 429 + body: { reason: "preempted_for_deadline" }.
- Eviction budget: limit number of evictions per tenant per minute to avoid thrashing.

Admission control and hold windows (concrete flow)
1) Request arrives -> attach metadata, compute expiration_time.
2) Check tenant/global quotas -> if over, mark as 'degraded' and follow degraded lane rules (sampled acceptance, increased hold to allow batching).
3) Insert into lane queue. For lanes with hold_ms, items are buffered up to hold_ms or until batch size threshold.
4) Scheduler runs at small tick (e.g., 4ms) and:
   - Picks ready batches where earliest expiration <= now+service_estimate(estimated_tokens).
   - For batches that would miss deadline, run preemption routine.
5) Dispatch batch to worker. If worker unavailable, try fallback to remote pool or degrade response.

Service time estimation
- Need a lightweight estimator for per-token latency given model variant and current GPU load. Use EWMA per route/variant keyed by sequence_length_bucket. Keep it <1KB metadata.
- service_estimate = model_dispatch_overhead + tokens * single_token_ms_estimate / parallelism_effect

Edge cases and notes
- Short-deadline short-token requests: should prefer to bypass batching (hold_ms=0) if deadline_ms < hold_cap; but small hold windows (10–25ms) can still win economically if high probability of other arrivals. Maybe probabilistic hold: hold_with_probability(p) where p adjusted by recent co-arrival rates.
- Cold KV-cache: if request requires a KV warmup that adds >30ms, adjust effective deadline or route to warmed pool. Could annotate request with kv_warmup_hint boolean.
- Canary / experiment routing: allow lane override that tags items not to preempt or to be served on canary-only workers.

Telemetry / invariants to track (observability)
- Missed-deadline count per lane/tenant + root cause tag (queueing, service, routing).
- Eviction count and avg requeue delay.
- Average hold_ms realized vs configured.
- Percent of requests accepted in first attempt vs degraded acceptance.
- Per-tenant token consumption and eviction budget usage.

Operator controls (console ops)
- Live tweak lane configs: hold_ms_cap, preemptible flag, admission polices. Changes should be dynamic with safe default rollbacks.
- Emergency mode: increase global reserved pool for interactive by seizing fraction of background capacity and marking background as preemptible.

Short prototyping notes (what I'll try next)
- Implement a tiny sim in Python to model arrival traces (Poisson + bursts) and test EDF vs priority-queue vs hybrid fairness. Track missed deadlines and cost (tokens).
- Implement simple EWMA service estimator keyed by (model_variant, token_bucket) and feed it into scheduling decisions.
- Wire up a preemption budget per tenant and test thrash scenarios.

Open questions
- Exact eviction policy: FIFO from tail of preemptible lanes? Or lowest-priority-by-estimated-cost? (I lean toward evict-lowest-utility where utility = importance_score / estimated_service_time.)
- How to coordinate preemption across multi-stage pipelines (eg, KV warm up + decode)? Need an end-to-end concept of 'work units' to evict safely.
- Should deadline_ms be absolute timestamp or delta? (delta is easier for SDKs, timestamp avoids clock skew if callers are distributed).

Sketch - ASCII diagram
[Ingress] -> [Global queue] -> {per-tenant queues} -> [lane buckets: interactive | background | batch] -> [scheduler + eviction module] -> [worker pools: fast | warm | cold] -> [model runtime]

Byline
Aisha — quick sketch for runtime scheduling RFC. Next: small sim + synthetic trace experiments, then prototype in local dev cluster.
